title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): X is a Riemann surface. P_X is the sheaf of local étale (locally biholomorphic) maps t: U -> P^1(C), i.e. projective charts, and H = PGL_2(C) acts on it. For two such maps, C(t,s) = (-2 s'''/s' + 3 (s''/s')^2) dt^2, with derivatives taken in the coordinate t. This is -2 times the Schwarzian derivative of s with respect to t, a section of omega^{⊗2}. It is invariant under H on both sides, it vanishes exactly when s and t differ by an element of H, and it satisfies the cocycle relation C(t,s) + C(s,u) = C(t,u). Consequently there is a sheaf Conn_X, an omega^{⊗2}-torsor (projective connections), with a map c^X: P_X -> Conn_X such that C(t,s) = c_s - c_t and H\P_X ≅ Conn_X. All of this is functorial for étale maps.

This page:
(1) On X_0 = P^1(C) the identity map is a global section of P_{X_0}, so c_id is a canonical global projective connection on P^1. It is the only one: projective connections form a torsor under H^0(P^1, omega^{⊗2}), and that group is 0 because omega^{⊗2} = O(-4).
(2) Hence for any X and any local chart t, c_t = t^*(c_can). The projective connection attached to a chart is the pullback of the unique projective connection on P^1.
(3) 'Extension to algebraic geometry': let X -> S be smooth (or formal) of relative dimension 1 and let t, s: X -> P^1_S be étale. The same Schwarzian-type expression defines c(t,s) in Γ(X, (omega^1_{X/S})^{⊗2}). One checks the cocycle and invariance properties 'by the same computation as in the analytic case'. Invariance is now under H_S = Aut_S(P^1_S) = PGL_{2,S}. This gives c: P_{X/S} × P_{X/S} -> omega^{⊗2}_{X/S}, where P_{X/S} is the étale sheaf of étale maps to P^1_S.
(4) The next page completes this: Conn_{X/S} is an étale omega^{⊗2}_{X/S}-torsor and c^X(t) = t^*(c). More generally, for a P^1-bundle X_0 over S carrying a unique projective connection, c(t,s) = s^*c - t^*c.
(5) Left margin: instead of differentiable/analytic notions, use the sheaf of principal parts (jets) of order ≤ 3, P^3_{X/S}, together with omega_{X/S}. This algebraizes the third-order Schwarzian.

Purpose: in this dossier (Gauss–Manin connections and Picard–Fuchs equations), this sets up the relative algebraic theory of projective connections, the Schwarzian side of uniformization and second-order Picard–Fuchs equations, so it can be used over arbitrary bases S, including characteristic p.
errors: The extension to an arbitrary base S is asserted 'by the same calculation as in the analytic case'. This is false as stated in positive or mixed characteristic. In characteristic p the kernel of the Schwarzian on étale maps is not a PGL_2-orbit: e.g. s = t + t^p has s' = 1 and s'' = s''' = 0, so C(t,s) = 0, yet s is not a Möbius transform of t. So property (iii) (C = 0 implies t = g·s) and the isomorphism H\P_{X/S} ≅ Conn_{X/S} need characteristic 0, or a formal / divided-power reinterpretation. The margin note on principal parts and 'schéma formel' may be Grothendieck sensing this.

In characteristic 2 the normalized expression -2 s'''/s' + 3(s''/s')^2 reduces to (s''/s')^2, so the theory degenerates. The integral normalization (multiplying the Schwarzian by -2) is defined over Z, but its properties are not uniform over Z.

The phrase about 'le faisceau H\P_{X_0} ... est le faisceau f-i(nal?)' cannot be right literally. H\P_{X_0} ≅ Conn_{X_0} is an omega^{⊗2}-torsor, not the final sheaf. Only its global sections reduce to a single point, because H^0 = 0. The reading is uncertain.

ideas.what: Projective connections on a Riemann surface as an omega^{⊗2}-torsor, with the Schwarzian derivative as the difference of two charts
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures / projective connections (sl_2-opers); Schwarzian as torsor difference
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); torsor formulation in Gunning, Lectures on Riemann Surfaces (1966); opers: Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the projective connection on P^1, since H^0(P^1, omega^{⊗2}) = 0; each chart's connection is the pullback t^*(c_can)
ideas.modern_name: Canonical projective structure on P^1; pullback of the flat PGL_2 structure

ideas.what: Relative algebraic version over an arbitrary base S: étale sheaf of étale maps X -> P^1_S, PGL_{2,S}-invariant integral Schwarzian, and the torsor Conn_{X/S}; suggestion to define it via principal parts P^3_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: Relative projective structures / sl_2-opers on smooth curves over a base (incl. characteristic p: Ihara's Schwarzian equations, Mochizuki's indigenous bundles, dormant opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1970s), Mochizuki (1990s), Beilinson–Drinfeld; Deligne for algebraic local systems / second-order equations

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck sketches the theory of projective connections for smooth relative curves over an arbitrary base S. This includes a torsor Conn_{X/S}, PGL_{2,S}-invariance, and generalization to P^1-bundles X_0 carrying a unique connection, plus a suggestion to work with jets P^3_{X/S}. He places it inside a Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs / Cartier-operation dossier, which hints at characteristic-p applications. The characteristic-p pathology of the Schwarzian is not addressed, and the thread stops at definitions.
missed.quote: Extension à la géom. alg. Soit maintenant X schéma ... de dim relative 1 sur un schéma S. Si t, s : X → P^1_S étales, on définit comme plus haut c(t,s) ∈ Γ(X, (ω^1_{X/S})^{⊗2})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the arithmetic theory of projective structures and opers in characteristic p (Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory, dormant opers, p-curvature of projective connections). Historically it shows Grothendieck linking the Schwarzian and projective structures with Gauss–Manin and Cartier/p-curvature themes. However, the content itself is standard and partly incorrect in characteristic p.

deep.surprise_reason: The analytic part is textbook material (Gunning-style torsor of projective connections, Schwarzian, uniqueness on P^1). The relative algebraic extension over arbitrary S is an early but unfinished sketch. It anticipates later work by Ihara, Mochizuki and Beilinson–Drinfeld without containing a new result, and its characteristic-p claim is overstated.
transcription_corrections: 'X schéma formel[?] de dim relative 1' is more plausibly 'X schéma lisse de dim. relative 1' (the image is ambiguous).
'faisceau H^1\mathcal{P}_{X_0}' should read 'faisceau H\P_{X_0}' (quotient of P_{X_0} by H), not a cohomology sheaf H^1.

'il y a une conn. projective can. C/ sur X_0': the circled C is Grothendieck's name for the canonical projective connection on P^1; later 't^*(C)' means the pullback of this connection, not of the complex numbers.
Left margin reads roughly: 'au lieu de différentiabilité, prendre l'extension ... i.e. P^3_{X/S} (principal parts) ... ω_{X/S} ... de degré ≤ 3', i.e. use jets of order ≤ 3 in place of derivatives.
